title: End a stalled run and spend its remaining budget on a new one
description: In spur-core/src/simulator/path.rs, track per run the last step at which any node's state token (State::node_state_token) changed or a client operation was invoked or answered. Keep, per session in the feedback store, the longest such quiet stretch observed in any run that later completed. Behind an opt-in config field stall_abort (default false, today's semantics), end a run whose current quiet stretch exceeds that session-derived length with a new end_reason 'stalled' in the runs table, treating it like iterations_exhausted for grading. The threshold is the session's own distribution, not a constant, and it starts unset so the first completed run sets it. Add util_stats counters termination.stall_aborts and termination.steps_reclaimed (steps the aborted runs would still have spent), so the mechanism counts its own firing. Enable it in scheduler_configs/loop/general_vr.json.
rationale: research/observations/TERMINATION_DEPTH.md: on a 229,980-run general chunk, runs that complete reach depth>=6 at 0.094 against 0.016 for runs that exhaust the step budget (5.8x, z 87) and depth>=8 at 8.5x, with deep runs ending at a median of about 1,100 steps against the full 6,000 for exhausted ones; in the plan corpus all 11 violating runs are among the 103 of 3,000 that complete, finishing in about 100 steps while the rest burn 10,000. About 97% of the plan corpus's budget and roughly 70% of the general chunk's went to runs that had stopped progressing. Ending those runs early turns their steps into new runs, which is events per explore-second by construction if per-run depth holds.
generalityArgument: A stall is defined by the absence of any state change on any node, which any protocol exhibits and none names; the threshold is derived from the session's completed runs rather than chosen. No handler, message, role or timer label appears in the rule.
notes: The per-run depth guards must hold: a run that is cut before its plan's later operations can be issued reads shallower, so the mechanism is expected to raise events per second without lowering per-run depth, and a per-run decline is the falsifier.

title: Lower timer admission at a node whose idle firings change nothing
description: Using the timer effectiveness counters (util_stats timer_effects, keyed by resume vertex, whether a delivery to the node was in flight, incarnation and inert streak), keep per session in the feedback store a Beta(fired, acted) per key, and per node within a run the count for the same key. In score_runnable, behind an opt-in config field timer_effect_steer (default false), apply a multiplier that lowers the priority of admitting another timer at a (node, resume vertex) whose firings with no delivery in flight have been inert against the session's distribution for that key, and never lowers - optionally raises - a firing with a delivery in flight. The multiplier reorders and never zeroes a choice. Add util_stats counters timer_steer.{evaluated, lowered, raised}.
rationale: research/observations/TERMINATION_DEPTH.md shows depth and violations concentrated in the runs that complete and the budget spent on runs that stall; GOAL.md names timer admission relative to delivery as the variable the plan corpora constrain (76% violation at full depth under admitted timers against under 2% in general mode). Whether the stalled runs are dominated by inert timer firings on idle nodes is what the timer effectiveness join measures; this hypothesis is the runtime use of that measurement and is only worth running once the join says idle inert firings predict budget exhaustion.
generalityArgument: The rule names no handler, message or label: it keys on the CFG vertex a timer wakes, on whether a delivery is pending for the node, and on the node's own recent effect history, and the threshold is the session's distribution rather than a constant. A protocol whose timers act is left alone by construction.
notes: Keep firings with a delivery in flight unpenalised: that is the race the oracle chain needs, and it is often inert on average. Measure the base rate of the gating predicate (idle and inert) before building, per GOAL.md rule 8.

title: Base rate of each score predicate at zero weight, and the flip fraction its derived weight would cause
description: With every steer_terms weight at 0 (today's evaluation template), read the steer_terms counters from the evaluation's utilization.json: per predicate (crash_after_timer_sends, crash_after_delivery_sends, stale_late, request_before_stale) the share of within-queue selections where it was present (present / decisions), the share where it was contested (contested / present), how many candidates it was scored on (evaluated), and the eligible-candidate histogram (eligible_hist). From the eligible histogram and the within-queue win table in PARAMETERS.md (section Steer terms) compute, per predicate, the fraction of selections its derived weight (2.33, share 0.7 of the queue roll) would flip. Report a table; change no behaviour. Kill criterion, stated up front per GOAL.md rule 8: a predicate present on more than 50% of the selections of its runnable kind (crashes for the crash terms, network deliveries for the other two) is not a gate, gets weight 0, and is dropped from the factorial campaign.
rationale: The score terms only earn a weight if their predicate is selective. The relaxation-gap ablation (research/observations/RELAXATION_GAP.md) says which orderings carry the bug; whether the corresponding predicates are rare enough to steer on is unmeasured, and a weight on a predicate that is nearly always true collapses into a uniform bias, which is how the timer-upweighting family failed.
generalityArgument: Reads counters only; names no handler, message or role. The predicates are defined over queue and ledger state that any protocol has.
notes: Counter: steer_terms.<term>.{present, contested, evaluated}, steer_terms.decisions, steer_terms.eligible_hist. Expected weak spot: stale_late's token conjunct may be near-universal because most deliveries write; if so the term is worth keeping only as sender-restarted, and the report should say so.

title: A 2^3 factorial over the three predicate weights, one campaign
description: Change only the campaign block of scheduler_configs/loop/general_vr.json: eight grid arms, one per subset of {crash_after_timer_sends, stale_late, request_before_stale}, each subset's weights set to 2.33 through the arm overlay (steer_terms.<term>: 2.33) and the rest 0, arm 000 being today's grid; allocation round_robin with min_slice_sec 12.5 (a 300 s chunk then gives 24 slices, three per arm; 30 slices over 8 arms leave two arms short) so a 300 s chunk gives every arm about three slices; reward unchanged. Per-arm depth and violations come from the runs table join the evaluator already does; an observations script computes the three main effects and the three pairwise interactions on depth>=6 per run and per second, with the A/A floor (depth>=4 stable to 0.1%, depth>=6 moving 7.5% on its own) as the bar. Guardrail: the router share is capped by the flip fraction the base-rate report predicts; any arm whose steer_terms.<term>.flipped exceeds a quarter of its decisions is reported as a schedule rewrite, not a preference.
rationale: The relaxation gap shows the bug needs three orderings at once, so the terms are expected to interact; a factorial over one campaign measures the main effects and the interactions in one chunk instead of three sequential hypotheses that each test one weight against the baseline.
generalityArgument: The arms differ only in numeric weights on predicates defined over queue and ledger state; no handler, message or role is named anywhere in the overlay.
notes: Counter per arm: steer_terms.<term>.{won, flipped, measured, acted}, steer_terms.authority_routed. Only after steer-term-base-rates has admitted the predicates; a predicate it dropped gets no arm.

title: Replace the purgatory delay rate with the stale_late preference: one arm
description: Add one grid arm to the campaign block whose overlay sets purgatory.delay_probability to 0 and steer_terms.stale_late to 2.33, beside the existing grid arm that keeps the delay rate at 0.15 with the weight at 0. Purgatory today delays 15% of all sends by a random duration; the relaxation-gap ablation says the ordering that matters is one stale-incarnation delivery landing after its receiver has moved on, which stale_late prefers directly and only when that situation exists. Read per arm from the runs table and campaign.json: P(depth>=5,6,7) per run, violations, runs per second, and steer_terms.stale_late.{present,won,acted} against purgatory.delayed_sends. Compare the new arm with grid and with grid-no-purgatory: if it is non-inferior to grid on depth>=6 per run and faster, the delay rate is doing no work the preference does not, and a follow-up ablate removes the delay_probability knob.
rationale: Six purgatory hypotheses added more holding and were falsified; grid-no-purgatory loses 40% of depth>=6 per run, so the rate is doing something, and the ablation says what: it sometimes lands a stale delivery late. A preference that acts only in that situation should keep the gain at lower cost and without a rate whose right value nobody can derive.
generalityArgument: The arm changes a delay rate applied to every send into a preference that acts only when a delivery's sender has restarted and its receiver has moved on, both of which any protocol with crashes has; no handler, message or role is named.
